description: On indefinite loan from the United States Air Force and the centrepiece of the museum's main hangar.
Composite airframe: ADF-Serials and Bob Ogden's museums guide record the museum's Sabre as A94-914 fitted with the rear fuselage of A94-921. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Ex-United States Army attack helicopter.

Served with 75 Squadron at Darwin; force-landed unmanned on the Ludmilla mudflats 27/05/1985 after the pilot ejected. Fitted with the fin salvaged from A3-105, restored at RAAF Base Tindal and returned to the museum by road 23/11/2005. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Crash remains held outside the museum. Crashed 7 nm east of Darwin 26/04/1984 after an undercarriage malfunction at night; the wreckage was recovered by Chinook A15-004 and its fin was fitted to A3-36. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Ex-RAAF Tiger Moth.
Wikipedia records this airframe by construction number 4373; no civil registration was established for it. Distinguished from the museum's other twins by being the only Dove on site.
Ex-RAAF 82 Wing, Amberley.
Homebuilt light aircraft; no registration recorded.
Wikipedia records this airframe by construction number 37; no civil registration was established for it.
Wreckage of the Model 21 Zero flown by Hajime Toyoshima and brought down on Melville Island during the first raid on Darwin, 19 February 1942.
One of few surviving B-25D airframes.
No registration recorded for this airframe.
Homebuilt canard; no registration recorded.
Full-scale replica representing the Spitfires that defended Darwin in 1943.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy; took part in the clean-up of Darwin after Cyclone Tracy. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Wikipedia records this airframe by construction number 3178; no civil registration was established for it.
Sold at the 2019 Grays Online disposal auction to a Broome owner, then donated and flown to the museum by Rhys Thomas in 2025. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.

Ex-RAAF 10 Squadron; ADF-Serials records it as retired to the Darwin Aviation Museum in 06/2018. It does not appear in the museum's public what's-on-display material, so its present condition and location on site are unconfirmed.
ADF-Serials records this Sioux as on display with the Aviation Historical Society of the Northern Territory, which operates the museum.

The Boomerang fuselage displayed inside the museum is based on the remains of A46-124, a deteriorated fuselage found on a property near Dalby, Queensland in the early 1980s. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Bare forward fuselage frame held in open storage at the museum. Served with 83 Squadron coded MH-Q and with 2 OTU. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
Cockpit remains and associated parts held in storage at the museum. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials.
